scandal.q: Where did Irene Adler hide the photograph?
options: In a recess behind a sliding panel, above the right bell-pull
Inside a book on the shelf
scandal.evidence: The photograph is in a recess behind a sliding panel just above the right bellpull.
scandal.hint: Think about what Holmes tells Watson after the cry of fire.

scandal.q: Why did Holmes arrange for someone to cry “Fire!”?
options: A person who thinks their house is on fire rushes to what they value most
To get everyone out of the house
scandal.evidence: When a woman thinks that her house is on fire, her instinct is at once to rush to the thing which she values most.
scandal.hint: Think about how Holmes explains his plan.

scandal.q: In the end, Irene Adler outwits Holmes. What does Watson say about it?
options: His plans were beaten by a woman’s wit
Holmes was beaten by bad luck
Holmes let her win on purpose
scandal.evidence: Sherlock Holmes were beaten by a woman’s wit.
scandal.hint: Think about the very last lines of the story.

red-headed.q: What sort of business did Jabez Wilson run?
red-headed.evidence: I have a small pawnbroker’s business at Coburg Square, near the City.
red-headed.hint: Think about how Jabez Wilson introduces himself.

red-headed.q: Why did Holmes think the assistant kept going down to the cellar?
options: He was digging a tunnel to another building
red-headed.evidence: I could think of nothing save that he was running a tunnel to some other building.
red-headed.hint: Think about how Holmes explains the case afterwards.

red-headed.q: Holmes thumped the pavement outside the shop with his stick. What was he doing?
options: Testing which way the cellar ran under the street
red-headed.evidence: Finally he returned to the pawnbroker’s, and, having thumped vigorously upon the pavement with his stick two or three times, he went up to the door and knocked.
red-headed.hint: Think about what lies under the pavement.

identity.q: What was strange about Hosmer Angel’s letters?
identity.evidence: “Not only that, but the signature is typewritten.
identity.hint: Think about what Holmes notices when he reads the letters.

identity.q: How did Holmes know Mary’s “father” was really her stepfather?
identity.evidence: “Your father,” said Holmes, “your stepfather, surely, since the name is different.”

identity.q: Holmes shows Mr. Windibank a typewritten letter Windibank sent. What is Holmes about to prove?
options: The same typewriter wrote Hosmer Angel’s letters
identity.evidence: “I think that this typewritten letter is from you, in which you made an appointment with me for six o’clock?”
identity.hint: Think about how a typewriter can give someone away.

boscombe.q: What call did the young man and his father use as a signal?
boscombe.evidence: When about a hundred yards from the pool I heard a cry of “Cooee!”
boscombe.hint: Think about what the son heard near the pool.

boscombe.q: The dying man said something about “a rat”. Why did that puzzle everyone?
options: It didn’t seem to make any sense
He said it in another language
boscombe.evidence: Witness: He mumbled a few words, but I could only catch some allusion to a rat.
boscombe.hint: Think about the son’s evidence at the inquest.

boscombe.q: At the pool, what did Holmes notice about the footprints?
options: Three separate tracks were made by the same feet
There were no footprints at all
boscombe.evidence: But here are three separate tracks of the same feet.”
boscombe.hint: Think about Holmes lying on the ground by the pool.

pips.q: What fell out of the envelope onto the plate?
pips.evidence: Opening it hurriedly, out there jumped five little dried orange pips, which pattered down upon his plate.
pips.hint: Think about the very first envelope.

pips.q: Why did Holmes think the senders were on a sailing-ship?
options: The letters came from seaports, with weeks between them
pips.evidence: “There is at least a presumption that the vessel in which the man or men are is a sailing-ship.
pips.hint: Think about where the letters were posted.

pips.q: What did Holmes think the weeks between a letter and its senders showed?
options: A fast mail-boat carried the letter, a slower sailing ship carried the men
The senders forgot to post it
pips.evidence: I think that those seven weeks represented the difference between the mail-boat which brought the letter and the sailing vessel which brought the writer.”
pips.hint: Think about how fast different ships travel.

twisted-lip.q: What did Hugh Boone do for a living?
twisted-lip.evidence: He is a professional beggar, though in order to avoid the police regulations he pretends to a small trade in wax vestas.
twisted-lip.hint: Think about how Holmes describes Hugh Boone.

twisted-lip.q: Why did Holmes bring a large bath-sponge to the prison?
options: To wash the beggar’s face and show who he really was
twisted-lip.evidence: Holmes stooped to the water-jug, moistened his sponge, and then rubbed it twice vigorously across and down the prisoner’s face.
twisted-lip.hint: Think about what happens in the cell.

twisted-lip.q: How could Neville St. Clair disguise himself so well?
options: He had been an actor and knew all about make-up
twisted-lip.evidence: When an actor I had, of course, learned all the secrets of making up, and had been famous in the green room for my skill.
twisted-lip.hint: Think about what he says about his past.

carbuncle.q: Where was the blue carbuncle found?
options: In the crop of a goose
At the bottom of a well
carbuncle.evidence: See what my wife found in its crop!”
carbuncle.hint: Think about what Peterson brings to Baker Street.

carbuncle.q: Why did Holmes study the old, battered hat so closely?
options: To work out who its owner was
To see if it would fit him
To find the stone inside it
carbuncle.evidence: A lens and a forceps lying upon the seat of the chair suggested that the hat had been suspended in this manner for the purpose of examination.
carbuncle.hint: Think about what Holmes can tell from a hat.

carbuncle.q: Holmes lets the thief go, saying “it is the season of forgiveness”. What does this show about Holmes?
options: He can be kind as well as clever
He didn’t care about the jewel
He was too tired to arrest him
carbuncle.evidence: Besides, it is the season of forgiveness.
carbuncle.hint: Think about what time of year it is.

speckled-band.q: What did the “speckled band” turn out to be?
speckled-band.evidence: Of course he must recall the snake before the morning light revealed it to the victim.
speckled-band.hint: Think about what Holmes explains at the end.

speckled-band.q: Why did Holmes think the ventilator was odd?
options: It opened into another room instead of to the outside air

thumb.q: What machine did the engineer go to look at?
thumb.evidence: This we have now been doing for some time, and in order to help us in our operations we erected a hydraulic press.
thumb.hint: Think about what the Colonel asked him to fix.

thumb.q: Why was it dangerous to stand inside the machine?
options: If anyone turned it on, it would press down on them
thumb.evidence: “ ‘We are now,’ said he, ‘actually within the hydraulic press, and it would be a particularly unpleasant thing for us if anyone were to turn it on.
thumb.hint: Think about what a press does.

thumb.q: The engineer wondered why anyone would need such a press for digging earth. What does this show?
options: He was starting to suspect something was wrong
He wanted to buy the press
He didn’t know much about machines
thumb.evidence: ‘The only point which I could not quite understand was what use you could make of a hydraulic press in excavating fuller’s-earth, which, as I understand, is dug out like gravel from a pit.’
thumb.hint: Think about what the engineer asks the Colonel.

noble-bachelor.hint: Think about the initials on the note.

She had never been married before

So he could take her with him
Because her father asked him to

beryl.q: How many beryls were in the coronet?

beryl.hint: Think about what the banker was told.

beryl.q: Why did Holmes go out to look at the garden alone?
options: Extra footmarks would make his job harder
He wanted to smoke his pipe
beryl.evidence: He went alone, at his own request, for he explained that any unnecessary footmarks might make his task more difficult.

Someone very heavy had walked past
